questions.question: Distinguish between an epidemic, a pandemic and an endemic disease, and explain how pandemics affect population.
questions.expected_answer: Epidemic: a disease affecting many more people than usual in one area at one time. Pandemic: an epidemic that spreads across many countries and continents. Endemic: always present in an area at a steady level. Pandemics cause sudden spikes in death rates, may lower birth rates for a while, lower life expectancy and can show as a dip or flattening in population graphs; they also disrupt economies.

questions.question: Describe how the Spanish flu reached and spread through South Africa and its effects.
questions.expected_answer: It arrived in September 1918 on troopships returning soldiers to Durban and Cape Town; it spread along railway lines to Kimberley, the Witwatersrand, the Free State and Eastern Cape, and migrant mineworkers carried it to rural areas. In Black October about 300 000 people died in about six weeks (about 6% of the population); families were devastated and many children orphaned. It led to the Public Health Act of 1919 and a Department of Public Health, but was also used to justify segregation (e.g. Ndabeni).

questions.question: Give two similarities and two differences between the Spanish flu and COVID-19 (for understanding).
questions.expected_answer: Similarities: both new viruses spread through the air; both came in waves; both overwhelmed hospitals; masks, closures and isolation were used. Differences: COVID-19 spread faster by air travel; the virus was identified quickly and tests existed; vaccines were developed within about a year (none in 1918); oxygen, intensive care and antibiotics were available; COVID-19 was most dangerous to older people, whereas the Spanish flu killed many young adults.
